turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about how you and your family have been. I will ask about several areas. I will ask about how you've felt physically and your feelings. I will ask about school and friends. I will also ask about information about sleep or taking medicine. We will make a summary of your responses to share with your medical team. Your team is your doctors and your nurses. It is also other people who work with you here. I'll just call them your care team. The things you tell us help the care team to know how to help you. If you ever need to share something urgent or that can't wait, make sure you call your care team right away, or have your family help you call.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I guess.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how you've felt physically. Have you had any problems with pain? What about sleep? What about nausea? What about your energy level?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My legs got really weak. I have to stop on the stairs and take a break.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that your legs are weak and you stop on the stairs. Anything else you want to tell me?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't run around at recess now. My grandma carries my backpack in for me.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Now I want to ask about your feelings. Have you felt sad, worried, grumpy, or lonely? Have you felt different from usual?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've been grumpy. My grandma keeps saying it gets easier in the next part, but what if it's worse? I think about that a lot.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that you are worried about the next part. How is schoolwork going? Have you been able to stay in touch with your friends? How are those things going?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm getting my work done, and I got a star on my reading. My friends don't really talk to me now, and they hang out without me on weekends.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that your friends are not talking to you as much. Have you had any difficulties with taking medicine, sleeping, eating, or using the bathroom regularly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I hate the pills at night. I take the last ones right before bed and they leave a taste I can't get rid of.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Anything else that you would like to share?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I still have to take the medicine before bed tonight. I just want to go to sleep instead of doing all that.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Okay, thanks for sharing all of that information. Now, I will make a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. I'm going to give everything a number. You can just let me know which numbers are most important. We can make them bold and put them at the top of the list. Okay, here's your list:
1. Feeling weak on the stairs
2. Worry about what happens next
3. Friends not talking as much
4. The bedtime dose at home
Which ones should we put on the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Number 2.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Here's your list:
1. Worry about what happens next
2. Feeling weak on the stairs
3. Friends not talking as much
4. The bedtime dose at home
Any changes?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Uh-huh. That one's right on top.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thanks for talking with me today. I hope your conversation with the medical team will help. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.
—
If anything urgent comes up between visits, make sure you call your care team right away. Your parent can help, if needed.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some specific questions about how you and your family are doing. I will ask about problems in a number of areas. I will ask about your child's physical health, how you are doing emotionally, family and social things, practical things, and how things are communicated with you and your child. We will share a summary of your responses with the medical team. We hope that this process will help with communication and ensuring access to resources. The medical team is your doctors and your nurses. They can address things and offer referrals and support services as needed. This also gives us information about how these services may be working for you. Then we know what we may need to change. If you ever have urgent or time-sensitive concerns between visits, make sure that you call your care team directly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how your child is doing physically. Have they had any problems with pain, sleep, appetite, or side effects of treatment?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He can't walk in from the parking lot without stopping twice, and he's on the couch from the minute he's home until dinner.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about how you and your family are doing emotionally. Are you noticing any problems with worry, sadness, anger or irritability? What about difficulty focusing? Or not feeling like yourself? Either for yourself or other family members.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'd call it worried more than sad. We're counting down to maintenance and I can't picture what he'll be like when we get there. The team has told us the plan; it's me that can't see it.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about family and social relationships. This is about you and your family. How are siblings doing? What about family conflict? What about social support from your family and community? Okay, how have family relationships and communication been? Any specific concerns?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nobody's at each other's throats, thankfully. My mother lives with us and my sister comes in most weekends, and those two get on fine.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about day-to-day activities. These are the activities involved with managing your family and your child's treatment. Are you having any difficulty with finances? What about child-care? What about transportation to the hospital or clinic?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Child-care takes care of itself. My mother is in the house with him all day, my sister covers the driving, and the bills are no worse than before. The bedtime dose is what beats us. He still drags it out an hour every night while I stand there, and on a dex week he argues over every step of it.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Finally, I would like to ask about how your care team shares information with you and your child. Do you have any concerns about how much detail you get? What about who gives you the information, or who is in the room for conversations?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nothing there that bothers me. The doctor goes over it as many times as I need, and she talks to him directly instead of over his head.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Any other items to add before I share your summary?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just the worry about the next phase. That's the one I carry around with me.
